verses.ar: وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَبُو بَكْرٍ صَاحِبُ الْغَارِ وَالصِّدِّيقِيَّةْ ۞ وَمِنَ الصِّبْيَانِ عَلِيٌّ وَمِنَ النِّسَاءِ خَدِيجَةُ الَّتِي ثَبَّتَ اللّٰهُ بِهَا قَلْبَهُ وَوَقَاهْ ۞ وَمِنَ الْمَوَالِي: زَيْدُ بْنُ حَارِثَةَ وَمِنَ الْأَرِقَّاءِ بِلَالٌ الَّذِي عَذَّبَهُ فِي اللّٰهِ أُمَيَّةْ ۞ وَأَوْلَاهُ مَوْلَاهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مِنَ الْعِتْقِ مَا أَوْلَاهْ
verses.tr: Wa-awwalu man āmana bihi mina r-rijāli Abū Bakrin ṣāḥibu l-ghāri wa-ṣ-ṣiddīqiyyah, wa-mina ṣ-ṣibyāni ʿAliyyun wa-mina n-nisā'i Khadījatu llatī thabbata Llāhu bihā qalbahu wa-waqāh, wa-mina l-mawālī Zaydu-bnu Ḥārithata wa-mina l-ariqqā'i Bilālun lladhī ʿadhdhabahu fī Llāhi Umayyah, wa-awlāhu mawlāhu Abū Bakrin mina l-ʿitqi mā awlāh.
verses.en: The first to believe in him among the men was Abu Bakr, the Companion of the Cave and the possessor of supreme truthfulness, among the young was Ali, and among the women was Khadijah, through whom Allah strengthened his heart and protected him. Among the freedmen was Zayd ibn Harithah, and among the slaves was Bilal, whom Umayyah tortured because of his faith in Allah, whereupon his master Abu Bakr bestowed upon him the great favour of emancipation.

verses.ar: ثُمَّ أَسْلَمَ عُثْمَانُ وَسَعْدٌ وَسَعِيدٌ وَطَلْحَةُ وَابْنُ عَوْفٍ وَالزُّبَيْرُ بْنُ الْعَوَّامِ ابْنُ الْعَمَّةِ صَفِيَّةْ ۞ وَغَيْرُهُمْ مِمَّنْ أَنْهَلَهُ الصِّدِّيقُ بِرَحِيقِ التَّصْدِيقِ وَسَقَاهْ ۞ وَمَا زَالَتْ عِبَادَتُهُ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَعَ أَصْحَابِهِ مَخْفِيَّةْ ۞ حَتَّى أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ﴿فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ﴾ فَجَهَرَ بِدُعَاءِ الْخَلْقِ إِلَى اللّٰهْ
verses.tr: Thumma aslama ʿUthmānu wa-Saʿdun wa-Saʿīdun wa-Ṭalḥatu wa-bnu ʿAwfin wa-z-Zubayru bnu l-ʿAwwāmi bnu l-ʿammati Ṣafiyyah, wa-ghayruhum mimman anhalahu ṣ-Ṣiddīqu bi-raḥīqi t-taṣdīqi wa-saqāh, wa-mā zālat ʿibādatuhu ṣalla Llāhu taʿālā ʿalayhi wa-sallama maʿa aṣḥābihi makhfiyyah, ḥattā unzila ʿalayhi ﴾fa-ṣdaʿ bi-mā tu'mar﴿ fa-jahara bi-duʿā'i l-khalqi ilā Llāh.
verses.en: Then Uthman, Sad, Said, Talhah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, the son of his paternal aunt Safiyyah, embraced Islam, along with others whom al-Siddiq gave to drink from the pure nectar of belief. His worship, may Allah Most High send prayers and peace upon him, together with his Companions remained concealed until there was revealed to him, “So proclaim openly what you are commanded” (15:94), whereupon he openly called the people to Allah.

verses.ar: وَلَمْ يَبْعُدْ مِنْهُ قَوْمُهُ حَتَّى عَابَ آلِهَتَهُمْ وَأَمَرَ بِرَفْضِ مَا سِوَى الْوَحْدَانِيَّةْ ۞ فَتَجَرَّؤُوا عَلٰى مُبَارَزَتِهِ بِالْعَدَاوَةِ وَأَذَاهْ ۞ وَاشْتَدَّ عَلٰى الْمُسْلِمِينَ الْبَلَاءُ فَهَاجَرُوا فِي سَنَةِ خَمْسٍ إِلَى النَّاحِيَةِ النَّجَاشِيَّةْ ۞ وَحَدِبَ عَلَيْهِ عَمُّهُ أَبُو طَالِبٍ فَهَابَهُ كُلٌّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ وَتَحَامَاهْ
verses.tr: Wa-lam yabʿud minhu qawmuhu ḥattā ʿāba ālihatahum wa-amara bi-rafḍi mā siwa l-waḥdāniyyah, fa-tajarra'ū ʿalā mubārazatihi bi-l-ʿadāwati wa-adhāh, wa-sh-tadda ʿalā l-muslimīna l-balā'u fa-hājarū fī sanati khamsin ilā n-nāḥiyati n-Najāshiyyah, wa-ḥadiba ʿalayhi ʿammuhu Abū Ṭālibin fa-hābahu kullun mina l-qawmi wa-taḥāmāh.
verses.en: His people did not distance themselves from him until he condemned their gods and commanded them to reject everything besides Divine Oneness. Then they dared to confront him with hostility and harm. The persecution of the Muslims grew severe, so in the fifth year they migrated towards the land of al-Najashi. His uncle Abu Talib showed him tender care and protection, and everyone among the people feared him and kept their distance from him.

verses.ar: وَفُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ قِيَامُ بَعْضِ السَّاعَاتِ اللَّيْلِيَّةْ ۞ ثُمَّ نُسِخَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى ﴿فَاقْرَؤُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةْ﴾ ۞ وَفُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ رَكْعَتَانِ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَرَكْعَتَانِ بِالْعَشِيَّةْ ۞ ثُمَّ نُسِخَ بِإِيجَابِ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ فِي لَيْلَةِ مَسْرَاهْ
verses.tr: Wa-furiḍa ʿalayhi qiyāmu baʿḍi s-sāʿāti l-layliyyah, thumma nusikha bi-qawlihi taʿālā ﴾fa-qra'ū mā tayassara minhu wa-aqīmū ṣ-ṣalāh﴿, wa-furiḍa ʿalayhi rakʿatāni bi-l-ghadāti wa-rakʿatāni bi-l-ʿashiyyah, thumma nusikha bi-ījābi ṣ-ṣalawāti l-khamsi fī laylati masrāh.
verses.en: Standing in prayer for a portion of the night was made obligatory upon him. Then this was abrogated by the words of Allah Most High, “So recite what is easy from it and establish the prayer” (73:20). Two units of prayer in the morning and two units in the evening were then made obligatory upon him. This was subsequently abrogated by the obligation of the five daily prayers on the night of his Night Journey.

verses.ar: وَمَاتَ أَبُو طَالِبٍ فِي نِصْفِ شَوَّالٍ مِنْ عَاشِرِ الْبِعْثَةِ وَعَظُمَتْ بِمَوْتِهِ الرَّزِيَّةْ ۞ وَتَلَتْهُ خَدِيجَةُ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَشَدَّ الْبَلَاءُ عَلٰى الْمُسْلِمِينَ عُرَاهْ ۞ وَأَوْقَعَتْ قُرَيْشٌ بِهِ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كُلَّ أَذِيَّةْ ۞ وَأَمَّ الطَّائِفَ يَدْعُو ثَقِيفًا فَلَمْ يُحْسِنُوا بِالْإِجَابَةِ قِرَاهْ ۞ وَأَغْرَوْا بِهِ السُّفَهَاءَ وَالْعَبِيدَ فَسَبُّوهُ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ بَذِيَّةْ
verses.tr: Wa-māta Abū Ṭālibin fī niṣfi shawwālin min ʿāshiri l-biʿthati wa-ʿaẓumat bi-mawtihi r-raziyyah. Wa-talat-hu Khadījatu baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin wa-shadda l-balā'u ʿalā l-muslimīna ʿurāh, wa-awqaʿat Qurayshun bihi ṣalla Llāhu taʿālā ʿalayhi wa-sallama kulla adhiyyah, wa-amma ṭ-Ṭā'ifa yadʿū Thaqīfan fa-lam yuḥsinū bi-l-ijābati qirāh, wa-aghraw bihi s-sufahā'a wa-l-ʿabīda fa-sabbūhu bi-alsinatin badhiyyah.
verses.en: Abu Talib passed away in the middle of Shawwal, in the tenth year of the Prophetic mission, and his death was a great calamity. Khadijah followed him three days later, and the trials upon the Muslims grew severe. Quraysh inflicted every kind of harm upon him, may Allah Most High send prayers and peace upon him. He then headed for Taif to call Thaqif, but they offered him no gracious response. Instead, they incited their foolish ones and slaves against him, and they reviled him with foul tongues.

verses.ar: وَرَمَوْهُ بِالْحِجَارَةِ حَتَّى خُضِّبَتْ بِالدِّمَاءِ نَعْلَاهْ ۞ ثُمَّ عَادَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ حَزِينًا فَسَأَلَهُ مَلَكُ الْجِبَالِ فِي إِهْلَاكِ أَهْلِهَا ذَوِي الْعَصَبِيَّةْ ۞ فَقَالَ: إِنِّي أَرْجُو أَنْ يُخْرِجَ اللّٰهُ مِنْ أَصْلَابِهِمْ مَنْ يَتَوَلَّاهْ
verses.tr: Wa-ramawhu bi-l-ḥijārati ḥattā khuḍḍibat bi-d-dimā'i naʿlāh, thumma ʿāda ilā Makkata ḥazīnan fa-sa'alahu malaku l-jibāli fī ihlāki ahlihā dhawī l-ʿaṣabiyyah, fa-qāla: innī arjū an yukhrija Llāhu min aṣlābihim man yatawallāh.
verses.en: And they pelted him with stones until his sandals were stained with blood. Then he returned to Makkah sorrowful, and the Angel of the Mountains asked him concerning the destruction of its fanatical people. But he said, “Indeed, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their descendants those who will turn to Him.”

verses.ar:
عَطِّرِ اللّٰهُمَّ قَبْرَهُ الْكَرِيمَ بِعَرْفٍ شَذِيٍّ مِنْ صَلَاةٍ وَتَسْلِيمٍ
اللّٰهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ وَبَارِكْ عَلَيْهِ
verses.tr:
ʿAṭṭiri Llāhumma qabrahu l-karīma bi-ʿarfin shadhiyyin min ṣalātin wa-taslīmin.
Allāhumma ṣalli wa-sallim wa-bārik ʿalayhi.
verses.en:
O Allah, perfume his noble grave with a fragrant scent of prayers and peace.
O Allah, send prayers, peace, and blessings upon him.
